card.name: Passive 'is/are' after a drug subject
card.fires_on: The helping verb 'is' or 'are' right after a drug or product noun, mostly in 'If a/an X is/are ...' clauses. It comes just before a passive verb such as being used, initiated, needed or inserted.

modes.label: If-clause with a drug
modes.description: 'is' follows a drug noun in a conditional clause, ahead of a passive verb like initiated or being used.
modes.example: If an opioid analgesic<< is>> initiated in a patient already taking a benz

modes.label: Plural subject in a dosing step
modes.description: 'are' follows a plural item such as vials, before 'needed' or a similar passive phrase.

card.writes: It favors past-participle verbs such as owned, installed or held and discourages -ing verbs, so a passive form is expected next.
card.plain: It fires on the 'is' or 'are' that follows a drug name in an 'if a drug is being used' sentence.
